claim: Assortative mating is the phenomenon whereby mates resemble each other more than would occur under random mating.
source: Assortative mating is the phenomenon whereby mates resemble each other more than would occur under random mating.
evidence: This is a definitional statement supported by established scientific knowledge and cited literature.

source: Through the lens of population genetics, assortative mating entails the correlation of genetic variants between mates (Versluys et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Versluys et al., 2021.

source: Assortative mating is often a consequence of a subdivided population structure, observed in most human populations (Cavalli-Sforza and Feldman, 1981; Nagoshi et al., 1990; Sebro and Risch, 2012; Sebro et al., 2017).
